distractors.reason: We don't say 'do a deadline'. 'Do' is used with tasks and activities: do homework, do the dishes, not with time limits.
We don't say 'make a deadline'. 'Make' is used with things we create, such as decisions, plans and choices.
We don't say 'take a deadline'. 'Take' is used with exams, breaks and photos, but not with deadlines.

example_sentence: Students must ___ a deadline for their Bagrut essays.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden traducir 'cumplir' como 'make' o 'do' y decir 'make a deadline' o 'do a deadline'. En inglés el verbo correcto es 'meet'.
explanation: In English, 'meet' is used with deadlines, requirements and expectations. To meet a deadline means to finish or submit something on time.

related_collocations.example: Every essay must meet the requirements of the exam board.
Students take their Bagrut exams at the end of the year.

memory_tip: MEET = arrive on time or satisfy (deadlines, requirements) | MAKE = create (decisions, plans) | DO = perform tasks (homework, dishes) | TAKE = sit an exam, take a break
